data.name: Bocadillo de Tortilla Francesa
data.description: A warm, tender plain omelet nestles inside a crusty bread roll, bringing together golden eggs, fragrant olive oil and a crisp crust for a simple, satisfying Spanish breakfast.

not_suitable_for: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease

refrigerator.notes: Best eaten freshly assembled. Refrigerate leftover omelet in a covered container within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 32°C (90°F), at 4°C (40°F) or below. Store bread separately to preserve its texture.

freezer.notes: Freezing the assembled sandwich is not recommended because the bread softens and the omelet can become rubbery.

storage.reheating: Reheat the omelet gently in a covered skillet until its center reaches 74°C (165°F), then place it in the bread.

items.name: crusty white bread roll
items.notes: One small baguette-style roll made with wheat flour, water, yeast and salt; choose bread without milk or butter.

items.name: egg
items.notes: Approximately 2 large eggs; weigh the edible contents without shells.

items.name: olive oil
items.notes: For cooking the omelet in a lightly coated skillet.

instructions.text: Split the bread roll lengthwise with the serrated knife on the cutting board, leaving one long edge attached as a hinge.
Beat the weighed eggs and salt in the mixing bowl with the fork until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.

doneness_cues.visual: Uniform yellow mixture without distinct strands of egg white.

instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in the nonstick skillet over medium-low heat for about 1 minute, until it flows easily across the base without smoking.
Cook the beaten eggs in the skillet for about 2 minutes, gently drawing the set edges inward with the spatula and tilting the skillet so liquid egg fills the gaps.

doneness_cues.visual: The underside is set and pale golden, while the top remains slightly moist.

instructions.text: Fold the omelet into thirds with the spatula to make an elongated shape that fits the bread.
Continue cooking over low heat for approximately 1–2 minutes, turning once, until the center reaches 71°C (160°F) on the instant-read thermometer and no liquid egg remains.

doneness_cues.visual: The omelet is fully set with no wet egg in the center.

instructions.text: Slide the freshly cooked omelet into the split roll and close the bread gently around it.
tips: Eat immediately while the omelet is warm and the crust is crisp.

troubleshooting.symptom: The omelet browns before its center is cooked.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The skillet is too hot or the folded omelet is too thick.
troubleshooting.prevention: Use medium-low heat initially and low heat after folding; spread the eggs evenly before they set.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the heat and cover the skillet briefly, checking frequently until the center reaches 71°C (160°F).

troubleshooting.symptom: The omelet feels dry or rubbery.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: It cooked too long after reaching its safe temperature.
troubleshooting.prevention: Check the center promptly after folding and assemble as soon as it reaches 71°C (160°F).
troubleshooting.fix: The texture cannot be reversed; serve promptly before it dries further.

chef_notes: A small skillet gives the omelet enough thickness to stay tender while fitting neatly inside the roll.
Beat only until combined; excessive aeration makes the omelet puff and then collapse.
Choose a roll with a crisp, thin crust and a soft interior so the bread does not overwhelm the eggs.
Cook egg dishes to 71°C (160°F) and reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F), following [FoodSafety.gov guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).
data.cultural_context: In Spanish cooking, tortilla francesa is a beaten-egg omelet commonly cooked in olive oil. Tucking it into a split bread roll makes a simple bocadillo suited to an everyday breakfast or quick meal, as illustrated by this [Spanish recipe reference](https://nutrium.com/p/jesuszubiri/recipes/523830).
